rationale: queens is a tiny (1.5 KB text, 4 functions) but compute-hot recursive backtracking benchmark, so the weight table prioritizes low-cost transformations and penalizes runtime-heavy ones: SUB and SPLIT get strong positive weights with low RuntimeCost/CorrectnessRisk weights because they cheaply obscure the arithmetic and basic-block structure of the hot solver loop without measurable slowdown; FLA and BCF provide the strongest control-flow hiding but their RuntimeCost weights (0.8/0.75) are set high so the selector only applies them where feature scores justify it, since flattening a tight recursive search loop would dominate execution time; IBR is kept moderate to obscure the branch-intensive backtracking decisions with tolerable overhead; ICALL and IGV are omitted entirely because with only 4 functions and a near-empty call graph their diversification payoff is negligible while adding indirect-call dispatch cost.
